name: Rehum
title: Persian official who opposed the rebuilding of Jerusalem
summary: Rehum was a high-ranking Persian official (chancellor/commander) in the province Beyond the River (west of the Euphrates) who actively opposed the Jews' rebuilding of Jerusalem. He wrote a letter to King Artaxerxes warning that the city's reconstruction would lead to rebellion, which temporarily halted the work.

keyEvents.title: Opposition to the rebuilding of Jerusalem
keyEvents.description: Rehum and other officials in the region opposed the Jews' efforts to rebuild Jerusalem and the temple after their return from exile.

keyEvents.title: The Letter to King Artaxerxes
keyEvents.description: Rehum, along with the scribe Shimshai and other associates, drafted a letter to the Persian king Artaxerxes warning that Jerusalem had historically been a rebellious city and that its reconstruction would threaten the interests of the empire.

keyEvents.title: Accusations of rebellion
keyEvents.description: In the letter, Rehum described Jerusalem as a wicked and rebellious city that had historically resisted great kings, claiming that rebuilding it would lead to lost taxes and revenue for Persia.

keyEvents.title: King's Reply Received
keyEvents.description: King Artaxerxes replied to Rehum's letter and confirmed that Jerusalem had a history of rebellion. The king ordered that the rebuilding work be halted until further notice.

keyEvents.title: Forced Halt of Construction Work
keyEvents.description: After receiving the king's reply, Rehum and Shimshai quickly went to Jerusalem and forcibly compelled the Jews to stop rebuilding the city.
